figures.before: What a CO Is and Why It's the Legal Finish Line
figures.alt: Inspection-ready renovation wall with organized framing, plumbing, electrical boxes, level, tape measure, and review folder
figures.caption: A certificate of occupancy depends on coordinated construction, completed inspections, corrected deficiencies, and documented readiness for use.

figures.alt: Commercial accessible restroom rough-in with clear floor area, fixture backing, and organized plumbing connections
figures.caption: Life-safety, accessibility, structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing inspections must be sequenced around the work that needs to be visible.

figures.alt: Commercial preconstruction worktable with blank plan sheets, ruler, clipboard, laptop, hardhat, and material samples
figures.caption: Inspection delays often begin with incomplete coordination, unresolved corrections, missing documentation, or work that was not ready for review.
